newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks under close govt watch for Mobutu cash.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks under close govt watch for Mobutu cash.

text.p: Swiss banks are under close government watch as part of a formal search ordered by the banking watchdog for any accounts they may hold of Zaire's ruler Mobutu Sese Seko, a Swiss official said on Friday.
Beat Frey from the legal assistance department of the Federal Bureau of Police Affairs said a state of "heightened requirement for attention" was now in effect for Mobutu accounts in Swiss banks.
This meant that "a withdrawal from accounts or the closing of accounts would probably not work any longer."
The embattled Zairean strongman, fighting cancer and a seven-month rebellion, left his capital Kinshasa on Friday amid intense speculation he may be heading for exile abroad.
Switzerland on Friday ordered a freeze on a luxury villa owned by Mobutu near Lausanne in response to a Zairean prosecutor demand but not on other assets.
Swiss media estimate Mobutu may have had up to $4 billion in Swiss banks.

The Federal Banking Commission this week ordered a formal search for possible Mobutu accounts among Switzerland's more than 400 banks and gave them until May 30 to report if they had any cash of Mobutu, his family or persons or companies associated with him.

Frey said the search means that if Mobutu called up and asked for his money, "Then probably the bank would call us. The probable effect is that it could work like a freeze, but it has not been formally ordered."

"No one has said 'We are ordering you not to do anything more now' and the banks are resisting, but rather one has told the banks 'Look, there is a problematic situation. If something comes up be careful. Don't make any mistakes,'" he said.
Swiss banking authorities say the Zairean ruler is unlikely to be holding much money in the Alpine country now and government officials deny close ties between the country and Mobutu.
But Swiss media has been revealing cosy ties between Mobutu and the Swiss to the contrary. Two government ministers even attended Mobutu's second wedding with their wives, Swiss television reported.
